title: Outline: section tree, moving sections and chapters, export bookmarks
instructions: Goal: a notebook with several PDFs shows one section per PDF in the bookmarks panel, with the PDF's own outline and the user's bookmarks inside; sections and chapters can be moved by dragging; the PDF export writes the same tree as PDF bookmarks. src/shared/outline.js already has mapPdfOutline (keep it and its tests). Read docs/NOTES-OUTLINE.md and src/shared/format.js (page and source fields) first. (1) Extend src/shared/outline.js with buildOutline(sources, pages, pdfOutlines). The bookmarks panel becomes a tree: one section per PDF in the notebook (in the order its first page appears), named after sources[key].name or the file name without '.pdf'; under it the PDF's own outline (pdfOutlines[key], already mapped with mapPdfOutline) and the user's bookmarked pages of that section in page order (title = bmTitle or 'Page n', n = 1-based position in the notebook). Pages that are not from a PDF (blank, ruled) belong to the section of the nearest PDF page above them; such pages before the first PDF page form a section 'Notes'. Return [{ kind: 'section', key, title, pageId (first page), items: [...] }] with outline entries { kind: 'outline', ... } and bookmarks { kind: 'bookmark', pageId, title }. Tests in test/unit/shared/outline.test.js: two PDFs, pages moved between them, bookmarks in both, notes before the first PDF, a notebook without PDFs (one 'Notes' section, bookmarks only). (2) Extend src/shared/outline.js with moveRange(pages, fromId, toIdExclusive, beforeId) and rangeOf(tree, entry). Dragging a section or chapter in the sidebar moves all its pages. rangeOf returns { fromId, toIdExclusive } for a tree entry: from its page to the page of the next entry of the same or a higher level (or the end). moveRange returns a NEW pages array with that run of pages moved before beforeId (null = to the end); pages keep their order inside the run; moving a run before one of its own pages returns the input order unchanged. Do not mutate inputs. Tests: move the second PDF section before the first, move a chapter inside its section, move to the end, no-op cases, and that buildOutline on the result still lists every bookmark once. (3) Extend src/shared/outline.js with outlineForExport(tree, pages). The PDF export will write the sidebar tree as PDF bookmarks. Return a flat list [{ title, level, pageIndex (0-based position in pages) }] in tree order; skip entries whose page is no longer in pages; titles at most 200 characters, never empty ('Page n' fallback); levels start at 0 and never jump by more than one from one entry to the next (clamp). Tests in test/unit/shared/outline.test.js. title: Scroll and zoom: frame-rate independent easing, wheel and pinch input, zoom anchor
instructions: Goal: zoom feels the same on 60 Hz and 144 Hz screens, a touchpad pinch follows the fingers, and the point under the cursor stays put. Today src/renderer/viewer.js (readable) eases zoom with a fixed factor per frame (zoom *= (target/zoom)^0.32), re-renders sharply 160 ms after zooming stops; zoom range 0.1 to 8. Read the zoom code in viewer.js so your API fits the call sites; do not change viewer.js. (1) (1) easeZoom(current, target, dtMs, tauMs = 60): the next zoom after dtMs milliseconds, moving geometrically (in log space) towards target so that the remaining log distance shrinks by exp(-dt/tau); returns target when the remaining ratio is within 0.4 %. Same result whether a 120 ms move is done in 2, 8 or 15 steps (within 1e-9 in log space). dtMs is clamped to 0..100 (a stalled tab must not jump). (2) wheelZoomFactor({ deltaY, deltaMode, ctrlKey }): factor for one wheel event: deltaMode 1 (lines) exp(-deltaY * 0.05), pixels exp(-deltaY * 0.0025), the result clamped to 0.5..2 per event. (3) isTouchpadPinch(e): true for pixel-mode events with |deltaY| < 40 (pinches send many tiny deltas and must be followed directly, not animated). (4) clampZoom(z) to 0.1..8. Tests in test/unit/shared/zoom-motion.test.js: step-count independence, convergence time for factor 2 at tau 60 ms (state it), clamping, line and pixel wheel events, touchpad detection. (2) Add anchorScroll({ zoom, newZoom, scrollLeft, scrollTop, pointX, pointY, pageX, pageY }): pages are laid out at pageX/pageY (screen units at the current zoom, scaled linearly with zoom, page positions given for zoom 1 as layoutX/layoutY: pageX = layoutX * zoom + gapX, pageY = layoutY * zoom + gapY, gaps fixed in screen pixels); the point under the cursor (pointX/pointY relative to the scroller's top-left) must stay under the cursor after the zoom. Return { scrollLeft, scrollTop } for newZoom, never negative. Document the formula in a comment. Tests: zoom in and out around the centre, a corner, a point on the second page with a fixed gap between pages, and a round trip (zoom 1 -> 3 -> 1 returns to the start within half a pixel). In the notes, list each place in viewer.js that should call which function. title: Scroll and zoom: render plan, pixel-budget cache and scroll velocity
instructions: Goal: long PDFs scroll without blank or blurry pages: pages on screen first, the next ones in the scroll direction prefetched, previews while moving, sharp pages when still, and a cache that never drops what is on screen. viewer.js (readable, do not change) keeps rendered pages in an LRU cache limited to 28 million pixels. (1) Add src/shared/scroll-velocity.js with createVelocityTracker({ windowMs = 120 }): add(t, y) records the scroll position y at time t (ms, increasing); velocity(t) returns px per ms from a least-squares line through the samples of the last windowMs (0 with fewer than 2 samples, or when the newest sample is older than windowMs at time t - the scroll has stopped); reset(). Keep at most 32 samples. Tests in test/unit/shared/scroll-velocity.test.js: steady scrolling, a stop, a reversal, irregular timestamps, many samples. (2) Add src/shared/render-plan.js with planRender(state). state: { pages: [{ index, top, height, width }] (screen px at the current zoom), viewTop, viewHeight, zoom, dpr, moving: boolean (scroll or zoom gesture in progress), velocityY (px per ms, + = down), cached: { [index]: scale }, maxCanvasPx: 16e6 }. Return an ordered list [{ index, scale, reason }]: pages intersecting the view first (by distance of their centre to the view centre), then up to 2 pages ahead in the direction of motion (velocity sign; both directions when |velocityY| < 0.05), then 1 page behind. Target scale = zoom * dpr, reduced so width*height*scale^2 <= maxCanvasPx. While moving: a page with any cached bitmap is skipped (the stretched bitmap is shown), and pages without one get scale * 0.5 (fast preview, reason 'preview'). When not moving: a page is listed only if its cached scale is outside 0.97..1.04 of the target (reason 'sharp'). Never list a page twice. Tests in test/unit/shared/render-plan.test.js for each rule, including a fast fling (velocity 3) and a huge page hitting the pixel cap. (3) Add src/shared/bitmap-cache.js exporting class PixelCache(budget, { onEvict }). Rendered pages are canvases; this pure class only does the bookkeeping by key with { px (pixels), scale, value }. set(key, value, px, scale) replaces an entry (calling onEvict for the old value unless it is the same value); get(key) marks it recently used; has, delete, clear (onEvict for all), size, used. When used > budget: evict entries not in the protected set (protect(keys) - the pages on screen) by oldest use first; never evict a protected entry, even if that leaves the cache over budget (report it with overBudget()). An entry larger than the whole budget is not stored (onEvict called at once, set returns false). Tests in test/unit/shared/bitmap-cache.test.js: LRU order, protection, oversize entries, replacing with the same value, clear. Also one test that drives all three together over a simulated fling across a 200-page PDF and checks the plan stays within budget. title: Reference reader: floating window bounds and split view layout
instructions: StudyNotes gets a reference reader: a PDF opens in a small always-on-top window to move, resize, scroll and zoom while notes are taken elsewhere, or is docked into the main window as one side of a split view (swappable); more documents come by drag and drop or from a folder. Windows, drawing and files are wired in by the maintainer. (1) Add src/shared/overlay-bounds.js. (1) clampBounds(b, displays, opts): b = { x, y, width, height }, displays = [{ x, y, width, height }] (work areas of all monitors), opts = { minWidth: 240, minHeight: 180, keepVisible: 80 }. Enforce the minimum size, then move the window so at least keepVisible px of its title strip (the top 32 px) lie on some display; if none, put it on the display nearest its centre (used after a monitor is unplugged). (2) snapBounds(b, display, threshold = 16): edges within threshold of a display edge snap to it. (3) resizeKeepingAspect(b, edge, dx, dy, aspect | null): resize from an edge or corner ('n','s','e','w','ne','nw','se','sw'); with an aspect (page width / height) the size follows it, the opposite edge or corner stays fixed. (4) defaultBounds(display, aspect): a quarter-width window at the right edge, vertically centred, aspect kept. Tests in test/unit/shared/overlay-bounds.test.js: two monitors side by side, unplugged monitor, snapping, every resize edge with and without aspect, minimum size. (2) Add src/shared/split-layout.js. State: { mode: 'single'|'split', ratio: 0.5, notesSide: 'left'|'right' }. Functions: layout(state, width, { minPane: 280, divider: 6 }) -> { notes: { x, width }, reader: { x, width } | null, divider: { x, width } | null }: in split mode the reader takes (1 - ratio) of the width on the side opposite the notes; the ratio is clamped so both panes keep minPane; below 2 * minPane + divider the reader is hidden (reader null, notes full width, state unchanged). dragDivider(state, width, x) -> new state with the ratio for a divider dragged to x (clamped as above). swap(state) flips notesSide. paneAt(layoutResult, x) -> 'notes' | 'reader' | 'divider' (wheel scrolling and Ctrl+wheel zoom go to the pane under the pointer). Pure, no mutation. Tests in test/unit/shared/split-layout.test.js: both sides, clamping, narrow window, swap round trip, paneAt at the borders. title: Android prep: file name rules and safe renames in one pure module
instructions: Goal: Windows and Android get identical, safe file and folder names, and renames that differ only in letter case work on both. Add src/shared/names.js. Desktop code cleans user-given names like this today: replace < > : " / \ | ? * and control characters with a space, collapse spaces, trim, strip trailing dots and spaces, prefix '_' to CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9 (case-insensitive), 'Untitled' when empty, at most 120 characters. title: Extension: formulas and formatting on paste, and on existing text boxes
instructions: Goal (user request): text with LaTeX such as '\[ \frac{400}{230}\approx 1{,}73=\sqrt{3} \]', copied from a chat, shows as a set formula; bold, headings and lists are kept. KaTeX CSS and fonts come from the katex package (see the notes for how the host loads package CSS). e2e: paste the formula above into a box, check a .katex element and no raw \frac text; double-click edits it; Ctrl+Z restores; the menu action converts an existing box; switching the extension off shows the $...$ text again.
